source.title: Partial Fusion of Neural Networks: Efficient Tradeoffs Between Ensembles and Weight Aggregation

record.tranche_reason: The study measures neuron- and channel-level activation distances across independently trained models, a different measure of shared representations from the claim's general representational convergence.
record.gate_note: The relevant reported results are the nearest-neighbor activation distances in Tables 10 and 11. The fusion, pruning, and accuracy results do not directly measure convergence as the claim defines it and are not included as rows. The paper also reports mean distances and conditional distances in Tables 8 and 9; these are not separate rows here because the reported cross-versus-within layer comparisons in Tables 10 and 11 directly summarize the similarity pattern.
record.test_reason: Appendix L compares nearest-neighbour activation distances within and across same-architecture networks trained from different seeds. This is a different method on V3's question: do independently initialised networks learn matching units or channels? The paper's main results (fusion and pruning accuracy) do not measure convergence. The Appendix L analysis is exploratory: one pair per architecture, no uncertainty reported.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right but ambiguous, because it says 'similarities' where the tables report distances. Correct reading: in early CNN layers, cross-network nearest-neighbour distances are smaller than within-network ones, so channels have roles shared across seeds. This reverses, less strongly, in deeper layers. The MLP pattern is very weak. The authors suggest layer- and architecture-dependent patterns can guide fusion versus pruning. Their main conclusion is that partial fusion and generalized pruning give efficient tradeoffs between weight aggregation and ensembles.
record.recipe_differences: The study measures Euclidean nearest-neighbor distances between activation vectors, rather than testing the Platonic Representation Hypothesis's cross-model representational geometry across increasing scale and capability.
record.method_sensitivity: The cross-versus-within nearest-neighbor distance pattern varies by layer and differs between the MLP and CNN examples.

fits_no_version.finding: Alignability by OT fusion rises with MLP width: at width 200 and above, fully fused models match the individual models. Naive-fusion accuracy is non-monotonic in width (Table 2).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Wider same-architecture networks trained from different seeds are easier to align neuron-to-neuron for weight fusion.

fits_no_version.finding: How well two ResNet18s fuse depends on training hyperparameters: with weight decay 1e-4 and 300 epochs, full OT fusion drops to about 80% (Appendix B.1).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: How alignable independently trained networks are depends on their training regime, not only on architecture and data.

record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 43rd International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 306, 2026
record.problems: The reported neuron-distance examples are limited to two MLPs and two CNNs trained on the same data with different seeds. The paper uses Euclidean activation distances and 1000 data points; it does not compare other similarity measures or out-of-distribution inputs. No uncertainty estimates are stated for these distance tables.
record.rows_left_out: No relevant result rows were omitted.

untested.parts: No scale sweep and no comparison across architectures, objectives or data.
No measure of shared subspaces, and no test of unit-level identity beyond nearest-neighbour distance. Only one model pair per architecture, with no seed variance.
OT and permutation kernels are used for weight fusion, but no representation-mapping loss or stitching is measured.
No interpretable features or circuits are examined.
No comparison of similarity measures, neighbour settings or out-of-distribution inputs. Layer variation is not a measurement choice.
No test of whether shared data or objectives cause alignment, and no plateau analysis.

missing.what: B→A cross-network nearest-neighbour distances, e.g. MLP layer 3 B→A 28.4, which exceeds both within values
Nearest-neighbour distances recomputed on the 80% least isolated neurons or channels
Distribution histograms showing unusually similar and unusually dissimilar neurons in most layers

record.verdict_notes: This is a fusion methods paper; the convergence evidence is a single exploratory appendix. It uses one model pair per architecture, Euclidean distances on activations from 1000 training points, and no uncertainty. Li et al. 2015 (an original source) is cited but not replicated. V6 and V7 links were removed from all rows.

versions.untested_parts: No sweep over model scale or capability, and no comparison across different architectures, objectives, data, or modalities as scale increases.
No paired image-caption data or vision-language model comparison.
The study measures activation-vector nearest-neighbor distances, not whether the same individual units differ or whether formal shared subspaces are learned.

The paper uses transformations for model fusion, but does not test whether one model's representations can be mapped onto another's with little representational or task loss by the mapping procedures named in this version.
No recurrence of interpretable features, neurons, SAE features, or circuits is tested.
Layer is varied and shows different cross-versus-within distance patterns. Other similarity measures, settings such as neighbour count, and out-of-distribution inputs are not compared.

The measurements concern models with the same architecture and training data but different seeds. The study does not compare shared versus different data or objectives, test scaling, or establish a plateau.

relationships.condition: VGG11 pair on CIFAR10, early conv layers 1–4 (strongest in layers 1–2)
relationships.reason: Cross-network nearest-neighbour distances are below within-network ones, so channels have counterparts in the other seed (T11-L1 to T11-L4).
relationships.display_finding: Cross-network nearest-neighbour distances were smaller than within-network distances, indicating channel counterparts across seeds, especially in the earliest layers.

source_check.label: supports
source_check.condition: VGG11 pair on CIFAR10, early conv layers 1–4 (strongest in layers 1–2)
source_check.reason: T11-L1 through T11-L4 show lower cross-network distances than both within-network baselines; the authors interpret this as evidence of corresponding channel roles across seeds.

relationships.condition: MLP pair on MNIST (all layers) and VGG11 deeper layers 5–8
relationships.reason: MLP cross advantage is very weak or absent; in CNN layer 5 cross equals within, and in layers 6–8 cross exceeds within (T10-L1 to T10-L3, T11-L5 to T11-L8). Kept as limits_scope because the within-network baseline measures redundancy, not absence of shared features.
relationships.display_finding: The MNIST MLP showed weak or absent cross-model advantage; VGG11 cross-model values equaled within-model values at layer 5 and exceeded them at layers 6–8.

source_check.reason: T10-L1 through T10-L3 show only a weak or absent cross-network advantage; T11-L5 shows approximate equality and T11-L6 through T11-L8 reverse the advantage. These qualify neuron-level matching across layers and architectures without establishing absence of shared subspaces.

relation.reason: The study reports its own within-network and cross-network activation comparisons bearing on V3.

tranche.reason: Appendix L directly investigates shared neuron or channel roles across independently seeded networks using Euclidean activation nearest-neighbour distances.

source_check.notes: Table captions sometimes call distances similarities; the numerical columns and Appendix L establish the intended direction. Absent and reversed row states describe the cross-network nearest-neighbour advantage over within-network redundancy, not absence or reversal of shared subspaces.
